clue.text: The rope was her undoing

indicators.note: undoing the words was and her unties them so their letters can be retied in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's downfall was brought about by a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undoing' signals an anagram of WASHER, the letters of 'was her'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick cable used for mooring or towing a ship is a kind of rope.

clue.text: Sufficient notice to treat as equivalent

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
to equate things is to treat them as equal

explanation.surface: An announcement is enough to put two things on the same footing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' is a newspaper advertisement, not attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough for the purpose; satisfactory without being more than is needed.

clue.text: Unpleasant spots on the roof

definitions.meaning: a painful viral rash of blisters
thin wooden tiles laid overlapping on a roof

explanation.surface: Ugly marks have appeared on the top of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the disease herpes zoster; the other is wooden roof tiles.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful blistering rash caused by the chickenpox virus, and overlapping wooden tiles covering a house top.

clue.text: Is roughly treated in a mischievous way

indicators.note: words that are treated are processed or worked on, so the letters of is and roughly are reworked

explanation.surface: Being handled roughly, someone responds with playful mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated', helped by 'roughly' in the surface, signals an anagram of IS ROUGHLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting like a rascal, playfully naughty, describes behaving mischievously.

clue.text: Art showing a packing-case

definitions.meaning: in old-fashioned English 'thou art showing' means 'thou ...', since to show someone how is to teach
a large wooden box first used for shipping tea

explanation.surface: An art exhibition is staged in a packing crate.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Art' as the archaic verb, as in 'thou art': 'thou art showing' is 'thou teachest', which split differently is TEA CHEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic second-person verb form meaning 'you instruct', and a plywood crate for shipping leaves from Asia.

clue.text: Charles Cole?

definitions.meaning: King Charles II of England, known by this nickname for his pleasure-loving court
Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme, who was a merry old soul

explanation.surface: Is someone called Charles really named Cole?
explanation.walkthrough: Charles II, restored in 1660, was nicknamed for his gaiety; the nursery-rhyme 'Old King Cole' was a merry old soul, a jolly king too. The question mark marks Cole as only a playful example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname of the fun-loving Stuart king Charles II, and a fair description of the jolly nursery-rhyme king.

clue.text: Sweet little gunners in a plane

indicators.note: in means the gunners' abbreviation is put inside the aircraft's name

parts.note: the Sopwith Camel was a First World War fighter plane
RA is the abbreviation for the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Some young soldiers share a sweet in an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals the short form RA (Royal Artillery); the Sopwith Camel was a famous British biplane. 'in' gives CA-RA-MEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy toffee made from heated sugar and butter is a type of confection.

clue.text: To remove, called in Italian family

indicators.note: in means the word for telephoned goes inside the family name

parts.note: the Este were a noble ruling family of Ferrara in Italy
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Someone phoned a family in Italy to get something taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: The house of Este ruled Ferrara and Modena; 'in' puts RANG inside it: EST-RANG-E.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate or drive apart, keeping someone at a distance, is to remove them in an old sense.

clue.text: Roman rock, misrepresented by a painter

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown falsely, so the letters of a painter are presented in a wrong order

explanation.surface: An artist paints a rock in Rome inaccurately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' signals an anagram of A PAINTER. The Tarpeian Rock on the Capitoline Hill was where traitors were thrown to their deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Name of the cliff in ancient Rome from which criminals were hurled, a famous rock of the city.

clue.text: Topping sweet sort of Geum found all round Ireland

indicators.note: the jumbled Geum letters are found all round the word for Ireland, placing it within them
a sort of Geum means the plant name Geum rearranged into another form

parts.note: Erin is the poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A gardener finds a variety of the geum flower growing all over Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' is the anagram signal and 'found all round' the container. Geum is a garden flower, also called avens; Erin is the old poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipped egg white and sugar baked crisp is often used as a dessert's crowning layer.

clue.text: Make provision about ringleader in the pit

indicators.note: about means the provisioning word goes around the leading letter

parts.note: to cater is to make provision of food
the leader, or first letter, of ring is R

explanation.surface: Someone organises supplies for the man who heads a gang hiding in a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' is not a gang boss but the first letter of 'ring'; 'about' puts R inside CATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bowl-shaped hole in the ground, as from a bomb or volcano, is a kind of pit.

clue.text: You can get bogged down in paper about the yearly gathering

definitions.text: You can get bogged down in

indicators.note: about here means the paper measure goes around the meeting abbreviation

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
AGM stands for annual general meeting

explanation.surface: Endless paperwork at a company's annual meeting leaves everyone bogged down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. A quire is an old paper measure of 24 or 25 sheets; the definition is a cryptic description rather than a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, wet marsh where feet sink is somewhere a person may be stuck fast.

clue.text: Stick to the demon drink …

parts.note: an imp is a small demon
ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone sticks to the devil's own drink, refusing to give it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like 'keep to', but it is a verb meaning pierce.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce or run through something with a sharp point is to stick it.

clue.text: … that's spilt around there, like spirit

indicators.note: around means the scattered letters go round the word there
drink that is spilt is scattered, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: following on from the previous clue, 'that' is the drink just named, ale
taken as written

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, the demon drink is spilt everywhere, leaving a ghostly atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 12-across, so 'that' is the drink just named there. 'spilt' jumbles it and 'around' wraps the jumble about the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Light, airy and otherworldly, as a ghost or soul seems.

clue.text: Gold short — bounder turns up and promises to pay how impudent!

parts.note: AU, from Latin aurum, is the short chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: turns up means the word for bounder is read upwards, in this down clue

parts.note: a cad is a bounder, an ungentlemanly man
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A cad who is short of money arrives offering IOUs; what cheek!
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses CAD to DAC, upward in a down entry; 'how' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold and cheeky in disregard of convention, as an impudent act is daring.

clue.text: Cat-calls where "Equus" was shown

definitions.meaning: the sounds cats make, read literally rather than as jeers
Equus is Latin for horse, and horses were once stabled in yards of this kind

explanation.surface: An audience jeered at the theatre where the play Equus was staged.
explanation.walkthrough: Equus is the play by Peter Shaffer about a boy and horses, which leads to theatres; but read as Latin for 'horse' it points to stables. Mews are rows of old stables, now often homes, in British towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises a cat makes, and a row of former stables around a yard, where horses were kept.

clue.text: Note: I washed up outside in the middle ages

parts.note: me, often spelt mi, is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: outside means the word for washed is placed around the letter I
up means the result is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: laved is an old word meaning washed

explanation.surface: A note: someone washed up outside, centuries ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the container and 'up' the reversal, since this is a down entry. Laved is an old poetic word for washed; the note is spelt ME in the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the period roughly AD 500 to 1500, the historical era between ancient and modern.

clue.text: Try to win a medal, and cut down forester

parts.note: to woo someone is to try to win their love
DSM is the Distinguished Service Medal

indicators.note: and cut down means the word and loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man woos, wins a medal, and fells a tree in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' trims AND to AN; the Distinguished Service Medal is a British military award.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who lives or works in the forest, felling trees, is a woodland worker.

clue.text: Listen to actor lament

indicators.note: listen to means the actor's surname is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Edmund Kean was a famous English actor of the early 19th century

explanation.surface: Pay attention to an actor delivering a mournful speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Kean was a celebrated Shakespearean actor; his name said out loud matches the verb for wailing over the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To wail in grief, especially over a corpse in the Irish tradition, is to mourn.

clue.text: Week-end change out of a winter woolly

parts.note: the end of the word week is K

indicators.note: change here means the letters of a and winter are rearranged

explanation.surface: At the weekend someone changes out of a winter jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'out of a', which the held clue lost. 'change' is the anagram signal; 'out of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes made of wool, such as a jumper, are known collectively in Britain as woollies.

clue.text: Race I would start to enter late in the day

parts.note: a race is a sporting event
I'd is the contraction of I would

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the word enter

explanation.surface: Someone says they would start a race late in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I would' contracts to I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: Ruffian takes my right place in the field

parts.note: taken as written
mid-on is a fielding position in cricket

explanation.surface: A thug muscles in and takes my spot on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: MID-ON is a cricket fielding position, near the bowler on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally one of Achilles' loyal warriors, it came to mean a hired thug or henchman.

clue.text: Man 'I ordered out is one revered by Indians

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of out are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A man ordered out of the room is someone the tribe holds in reverence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' is the anagram signal, working only on 'out'. A manitou is a spirit of Algonquian belief in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit or supernatural power worshipped by Algonquian peoples of North America.

clue.text: Element I love to eat

parts.note: love is a score of nil in tennis, so it gives O
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone declares fondly that their passion is eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is zero in tennis, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical substance with atomic number 53, one of the halogens.

clue.text: One bed in nine is a hazard to health

indicators.note: in means the numeral and the small bed are put inside the word nine

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: One bed out of every nine is found to be unsafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'One' as a capitalised word is the Roman numeral I, not a count.
explanation.definitionFit: The addictive drug in tobacco, which damages the body.

clue.text: Throws out several skips

parts.note: V, the Roman numeral five, stands for a handful or several
to skip a thing is to omit it, leave it out

explanation.surface: Someone throws away a number of skipping ropes, or misses several turns.
explanation.walkthrough: V is five in Roman numerals, a stand-in for 'several'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up food from the stomach is to throw it up, a slang sense of throw out.

clue.text: Cecilia Salisbury was here

parts.note: it looks like a woman's name, but split as Cecil plus ia, swap Cecil for the surname of the empire builder Cecil and add ia; Salisbury was this country's capital

explanation.surface: A woman called Cecilia Salisbury once visited this place.
explanation.walkthrough: Cecil Rhodes gave his name to the former colony; replace 'Cecil' in 'Cecilia' with his surname. Its capital Salisbury is now Harare, in Zimbabwe.
explanation.definitionFit: The former British colony in southern Africa, named after Cecil Rhodes, now called Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Lydia's left with a lot of pain

definitions.note: the definition is a possessive, meaning Lydia's surname

parts.note: anguish is great pain or distress

explanation.surface: A woman named Lydia is left in great suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: Lydia Languish is the romantic heroine of Sheridan's 18th-century comedy The Rivals; the clue asks for her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Surname of the heroine of Sheridan's play The Rivals, so it is the name belonging to her.

clue.text: Fallen stones to the North give shelter

parts.note: scree is loose stones fallen on a mountain slope
N is the abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: A rockfall on the north side offers walkers some protection.
explanation.walkthrough: SCREE is the loose broken rock below a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: To shield or protect something from view or harm is to give it cover.
